result.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
result.summary: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 研究去中心化在线学习中的 network regret：构造两节点反例说明 gossip 类算法即使分歧有界也可能产生指数级 regret，并提出每轮仅一次邻居通信的黑箱归约以获得次线性 comparator-adaptive network regret。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「通信预算—regret」权衡与有界分歧仍失效的反例，可能为多智能体/并行 latent 状态的有限通信协调、以及用 regret 类信号决定推理是否停止提供分析视角；但本文不含视觉或多模态环节，迁移价值需核查。
